subject.title: [Bug]: Lane remains occupied after reply emitted during failover — blocks subsequent inbound messages

question: Should OpenClaw release or adopt same-session lane ownership after durable visible reply delivery while provider failover/backend cleanup continues, and what transcript and ordering guards must gate that handoff?
rationale: The source path is clear enough to show why follow-ups wait, but choosing the release point changes session ordering, transcript durability, provider cleanup, and channel delivery semantics.

options.title: Delivery-Gated Handoff
options.body: Release or transfer same-session admission after durable visible delivery, with explicit guards for transcript persistence, final delivery, and follow-up ordering.

options.title: Keep Run-Held Lane
options.body: Keep the lane occupied until backend/run settlement and improve busy/failover feedback instead of changing ownership semantics.

options.title: Fold Into Run-Lifecycle Design
options.body: Defer this specific fix into the broader run-lifecycle reliability work so terminal release, stale takeover, and delivery handoff are designed together.

recommendation.title: Delivery-Gated Handoff
recommendation.body: Release or transfer same-session admission after durable visible delivery, with explicit guards for transcript persistence, final delivery, and follow-up ordering.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent reply delivery and session-management history makes this the best available routing owner for the product semantics decision.
